summary.prose: In JetBrains, the Model tiers settings section keeps editing the three global tiers, but every runner, model and effort it offers now comes from the daemon's model definitions; the plugin keeps no list of its own. A model the daemon does not list can be checked through its CLI from the section; the results are shown per effort level, and the model becomes selectable only after the user approves it and the daemon restarts. The per-repo settings keep only the role-to-tier choices and coreFloor. A save that needs a daemon restart offers one.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: The curated cloud catalog keeps its file (src/assets/models/cloud-model-catalog.json), its loader (validateModelCatalog, src/daemon/model-catalog.ts:162) and its boot hook (src/daemon/index.ts:381), as the DEF decided, and is extended in place; the boot hook moves ahead of the settings reconcile and the worker threads, because the settings defaults now come from the file. The file is extended into the model definitions: exactly one entry for each built-in family, each with its CLI kind (CLI families), its selectable models with aliases, accepted efforts and input limit, its tier defaults and summariser model (CLI families), the Ollama tool-loop default, and the default family. Each Ollama model's input limit is its context window and replaces the global models.shaper.ollamaNumCtx; the output cap ollamaNumPredict stays global. A ModelRegistry built from the file and the per-user approved-model store answers every model question in the daemon; each thread builds it on first use and caches it, the way it loads and caches settings today (src/config/analyze.ts:234). A daemon restart guarantees that every thread uses a changed file, approval or saved tier; until then, a thread that starts or first reads them after the change, such as a worker the supervisor replaces after a crash (src/daemon/threads/supervisor.ts:136-148), may already use it, as with settings today. That is harmless: every saved tier has passed config.write's checks and every approval a check in which the model ran. The settings catalog takes the defaults of its tier runner, tier model and local coreModel rows, and the allowed effort values, from the same file, so reconcile, the updater, the settings catalog loader and older plugins keep working unchanged and no model name stays in code. One read-only request, models.definitions, serves the definitions to clients and is the source of providers.listModels; models.resolveRole lets the TUI's review command run the model the daemon would. Unknown Claude and Codex models are checked through their CLI one call at a time and recorded only on the user's approval, and only for a check in which the model ran. A tier set to a model that is neither listed nor approved runs a tier default with a warning (decision A). Tiers become global-only; a repo keeps `tasks` and coreFloor. Every Story leaves the build and tests passing, keeping a named stopgap for anything a later Story migrates. Settings-write safety is out of scope (ISSUE-8dc75bc5).

consumedContracts.name: models.definitions IPC request
consumedContracts.purpose: The one read-only request clients use to learn the definitions (k2): families with CLI kind and rejected ids, models with aliases, efforts and limits and whether they are shipped or user-approved, tier defaults, summariser model, tool-loop default, default family, and each listed Ollama model's installed state. providers.listModels is drawn from the same registry (s2/ac2).

consumedContracts.name: Unknown-model check and approval requests
consumedContracts.purpose: Checks a Claude or Codex model that is not in the definitions through its CLI, one call at a time (k1, k3), returns per-effort evidence, and records the user's decision as an ApprovedProfile (sc2) outside the shipped file and config.json (k4, k5). Approval is accepted only for a check in which the model ran without error. A decision applies at the next daemon restart, which the result says. Ollama has no such flow: only listed Ollama models are selectable.

consumedContracts.name: Settings rules and models.resolveRole
consumedContracts.purpose: What changes in settings: the settings catalog's tier runner, tier model and local coreModel defaults and the allowed effort values come from the definitions; per-repo tier overrides are removed with a warning (k6, s3/ac5); ollamaNumCtx is pruned; config.write refuses a tier set to a rejected model (s4/ac4) and reports restartRequired for model settings. models.resolveRole gives the TUI's review command the tier, model, effort and provider settings the daemon would use for a role and repo.

boundary.internal: The JetBrains model-tiers section driven by models.definitions instead of ModelTiersModel.PROVIDERS; the unknown-model check and approval dialog; the per-repo settings without per-tier fields; showing restartRequired. Tests: the section offers exactly a fake answer's options and the plugin keeps no runner or model list (ac1); an unknown model is saved only after approval (ac2); the per-repo settings show only `tasks` and coreFloor (ac3).

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Extending the catalog file, its types (CloudModelCatalogFile, src/daemon/model-catalog.ts:48) and its validator in place; refreshing its contents with today's models, the aliases today's tier defaults use (opus, sonnet, haiku), the Ollama models insrc ships with and their context windows, and today's coreModel as the tool-loop default; the registry and its per-thread cache; moving the boot validation ahead of the settings reconcile and the worker threads; reading the approved-model store (a malformed store is logged and treated as empty); keeping the curated catalog's existing accessor answering providers.listModels from the new file shape until s2 replaces it. The validator refuses a missing or malformed file, an unknown, missing or repeated family, a CLI family without its CLI kind, tier defaults or summariser model, a model without an efforts list, a duplicate id or alias, a default that is not a model of its family, an Ollama model without a token input limit, and a tool-loop default that is not listed, naming the entry (ac3). Tests: one fixture per refusal reason (ac3); a model and alias added to a fixture are served after a restart with no code change (ac2); the file is validated before the settings reconcile, before any worker starts and before listen (ac1, k7); repeated requests in one thread return the same definitions even after the file changes on disk (ac1); a replacement worker started after the file, the store or config.json changed on disk uses the new values while a surviving thread keeps its own until the restart, and a thread whose first read comes after such a change likewise uses the new values; after a daemon restart every thread resolves the same definitions, approvals and tiers; providers.listModels still returns today's Claude and Codex models through the kept accessor; alias, effort and limit lookups; resolveTier distinguishes rejected-model from unlisted-model and falls back to the tier's family default, or the default family's for an Ollama tier.

The models.definitions handler and its method-class entry, the projection of the registry, each listed Ollama model's installed state from the existing bounded listing, and re-sourcing providers.listModels from the registry (for Ollama, listed models only), then removing the curated catalog accessor s1 kept. Tests: models.definitions returns every field of a fixture file (ac1); providers.listModels and models.definitions agree for every family, and an installed but unlisted Ollama model appears in neither (ac2); with Ollama not answering, installed is absent and the request still succeeds.

Moving every daemon consumer onto the registry: tier resolution, summariser selection, effort forwarding, CliProvider's input budget and CLI kind, OllamaProvider's num_ctx, the tool-loop model (an unlisted coreModel runs the tool-loop default with a warning) and the runner and model literals in routing, provider construction, attribution and workflow code; SUMMARISER_CLI_FALLBACK, CODEX_INPUT_BUDGET_CHARS and ollamaNumCtx go; DEFAULT_TIERS and TIER_EFFORTS stop being written in code and remain only as temporary exports drawn from the definitions for the TUI's model-tiers pane, which s5 migrates; no daemon code uses them. The settings catalog's tier and coreModel defaults and effort values are taken from the definitions; how the settings catalog reaches the file is decided in this Story's LLD and must work in every process that loads the settings catalog today (the daemon, the TUI, the updater, and the VS Code bundle until s6 drops its use). Reconcile removes per-repo tier overrides with a warning and prunes ollamaNumCtx; readRepoOverride and its callers go. config.write refuses a tier set to a rejected model and reports restartRequired. models.resolveRole and its method-class entry. Both installer copies take tier defaults and the tool-loop default from the file. Tests: an unset tier resolves to the file's default, and with a fixture whose defaults differ from today's, reconcile fills the fixture's values (ac1); an unsupported effort is dropped with a warning naming model and effort (ac2); a source scan fails on runner or model literals outside the family implementations, on any read of ollamaNumCtx, and on any daemon use of the temporary DEFAULT_TIERS or TIER_EFFORTS exports (ac3); the TUI still builds and its model-tiers pane shows the definitions' defaults; a repo's `tasks` choice applies with the global tier's model (ac4); reconcile removes per-repo tier overrides with a warning naming repo and tier and keeps `tasks` and coreFloor (ac5); an unlisted model falls back with the warning (decision A); a fixture Ollama model's input limit sets num_ctx; config.write refuses a rejected model and reports restartRequired; models.resolveRole matches the daemon's own resolution for a CLI tier and an Ollama tier; the settings catalog loader accepts the catalog and an unset JetBrains tier still shows the default family's values.

The per-family check procedures (Codex: the CLI's model list plus a run; Claude: a run, the input limit from the JSON output, recognised effort names), run one call at a time; telling a reachable CLI that refuses the model apart from an unreachable CLI; refusing approval unless the model ran without error; writing the store atomically and acknowledging a decision only once it is written; the method-class entries. Tests: checks against fake CLIs record each verdict and run one at a time (ac1); results list each claimed level with evidence and nothing is usable before approval (ac2); after approval and a restart only the approved levels are accepted (ac3); a rejected profile or unreachable CLI refuses the model with a reason, and approving a check whose model did not run is refused (ac4); after a restart an approved model appears in models.definitions as user-approved and a rejected one among the rejected ids (ac5); a failed store write returns write-failed and keeps the previous store.

The TUI model-tiers pane and its effort choices from models.definitions, removing the temporary DEFAULT_TIERS and TIER_EFFORTS exports s3 kept; the unknown-model check and approval screen; the repo settings view limited to `tasks` and coreFloor; showing restartRequired and offering maintenance.restart; the review command using models.resolveRole and building its provider from the answer instead of reading config.json; Setup recommending the definitions' tool-loop default instead of DEFAULT_LOCAL_MODEL, and saying it cannot recommend when the daemon is not running. Tests: the pane offers exactly the options of a fake models.definitions answer and no source file still exports or imports DEFAULT_TIERS or TIER_EFFORTS (ac1); saving an unknown model starts the check and shows its results (ac2); the repo view edits only `tasks` and coreFloor (ac3); the review command runs the model a fake models.resolveRole returns for a CLI and an Ollama tier; Setup recommends the fake answer's tool-loop default.

The VS Code model-tier picker driven by models.definitions instead of its runner list and the bundled settings catalog's effort rows, removing the bundle's import of the settings catalog; the unknown-model check and approval prompt; the Repo Configuration panel without per-tier fields; showing restartRequired and offering insrc.daemon.restart. Tests: the picker offers exactly a fake answer's options and the bundle keeps no runner or model list (ac1); an unknown model is saved only after approval (ac2); the repo panel shows only `tasks` and coreFloor (ac3).

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase D — clients render the daemon's definitions

nonFunctional.performance: The file is parsed once per thread and every model question is an in-memory lookup; models.definitions touches no CLI and makes one bounded Ollama listing call, the same one providers.listModels makes today.
nonFunctional.security: No cloud REST call is added (k1): checks run only through the installed claude and codex CLIs. The approved-model store is a per-user file under the insrc home written only by the daemon; clients reach it only through models.approve and models.reject (k2).
nonFunctional.observability: A bad file stops the daemon with a log naming the entry (s1/ac3); a dropped effort logs model and effort (s3/ac2); a tier fallback logs tier, requested model, reason and the default used (decision A); a tool-loop substitution logs both models; removing a per-repo tier override logs repo and tier (s3/ac5); each CLI call of a check and its verdict is logged.
nonFunctional.durability: Approved and rejected profiles live outside the shipped file and config.json, so they survive restarts and updates; the store is replaced atomically and a decision is acknowledged only once written; a malformed store is logged and treated as empty. When an update ships a model the user had approved, the shipped definition wins. Existing `tasks`, coreFloor, ollamaNumPredict and every tier value already in config.json are kept. Between a change and the next restart, threads may differ (a replaced worker or a late first read uses the new values); the restart brings them together.

api.name: DaemonGateway.modelDefinitions

returns.meaning: Loaded(ModelDefinitionsDto) parsed from models.definitions (families with id, cliKind?, displayName, tierDefaults, toolLoopModel?, models with id, aliases, displayName?, efforts, source, installed?; defaultFamily), or Failed(DaemonFailure). A malformed family or model entry is skipped; an answer with no families is Failed(other).

errors.condition: DaemonUnavailableException — which UnixSocketDaemonRpc.call throws for ANY socket I/O failure, at connect or mid-call; the text therefore says 'the daemon is not running or the connection was lost'. A clean early end of the reply (empty/unparseable) is Other
the reply's error starts with 'unknown method: '; the text says to update the daemon
any other framed error, malformed reply or transport fault, shown as it is

postconditions: Declared on the DaemonGateway interface and implemented in DaemonGateway.kt; DaemonGatewayService (jetbrains-plugin/src/main/kotlin/ai/insors/insrc/jetbrains/daemon/DaemonGatewayService.kt) forwards modelDefinitions, checkModel and decideModel to its delegate like its other methods, and the test fakes that implement DaemonGateway (lifecycle/DaemonLifecycleServiceTest.kt, onboarding/OnboardingLifecycleTest.kt, onboarding/OnboardingCleanupIntegrationTest.kt, onboarding/OnboardingWiringTest.kt) gain 'not used in this test' stubs

api.name: DaemonGateway.checkModel
api.signature: fun checkModel(family: String, modelId: String, claimedEfforts: List<String>): ModelCheckOutcome

parameters.name: family
parameters.purpose: a CLI family id taken from the definitions

parameters.name: modelId
parameters.purpose: the unlisted model the user typed

parameters.name: claimedEfforts
parameters.purpose: the effort levels to try (the union of the family's served efforts, as s6)

returns.meaning: Checked(checkId, runs, inputLimit?, efforts[effort, verdict, evidence], error?) — INCLUDING a check that did not run, whose result carries error alongside checkId and efforts — or Failed(DaemonFailure); an invalid-params reply ({error, recoverable:false} with no checkId) is Failed(Other) with the daemon's text

preconditions: called off the EDT (the check runs the CLI and can take minutes)

The reply is read through DaemonRpc.call(method, params, resultErrorIsFailure = false), so a ModelCheckResult's own `error` field is not mistaken for the structured-failure convention; the gateway itself tells a check result (has checkId) from an invalid-params reply (no checkId)

api.name: DaemonGateway.decideModel
api.signature: fun decideModel(checkId: String, approve: Boolean, efforts: List<String>): ModelDecisionResult

parameters.name: approve
parameters.purpose: models.approve when true, models.reject when false

parameters.name: efforts
parameters.purpose: the efforts the user allows (approve only); never a rejected one

returns.meaning: Recorded (restart required) | Refused(reason, detail) carrying the daemon's reason ('unknown-check' | 'model-did-not-run' | 'invalid-efforts' | 'write-failed') | Failed(DaemonFailure)

postconditions: Never throws; an 'unknown-check' tells the user to check again

api.name: DaemonRpc.call (result-error flag)
api.signature: fun call(method: String, params: Map<String, Any?>, resultErrorIsFailure: Boolean): DaemonResult = call(method, params)

parameters.name: resultErrorIsFailure
parameters.purpose: false keeps a non-empty result.error in DaemonResult.data instead of turning the reply into ok=false

returns.meaning: With true (and through the existing two-argument call) exactly today's parse; with false, a top-level error still fails, but an object result is returned whole in data even when it has an error field

postconditions: A default method on the interface, so existing DaemonRpc fakes are untouched; UnixSocketDaemonRpc overrides it with parse(reply, resultErrorIsFailure)
Every existing caller keeps the structured-error behaviour (jetbrains-plugin/src/main/kotlin/ai/insors/insrc/jetbrains/daemon/UnixSocketDaemonRpc.kt parse)

api.name: SaveResult (extended)
api.signature: sealed interface SaveResult { data class Saved(val restartRequired: Boolean = false); data class Rejected(val reason: String, val detail: String? = null); data class Unavailable(val reason: String) }

returns.meaning: config.write's own answer carried through: restartRequired on success, reason ('invalid-path' | 'rejected-model' | 'per-repo-tier' or framed error) and detail on refusal

postconditions: Every existing caller (ModelTiersSection, PerRoleSection, PerRepoSection, InsrcSettingsConfigurable) matches `is SaveResult.Saved` and shows detail when present

api.name: ModelTiersModel (reshaped)

parameters.name: catalog
parameters.purpose: the configured tier leaves (currentValue / isSet of models.tiers.<tier>.runner|model|effort)

parameters.name: definitions
parameters.purpose: the only source of runner, model and effort choices and of defaults

returns.meaning: runnerOptions = the definitions' families; modelOptions(tier) = the runner family's models (alias and 'not installed' shown in the label; a configured model the definitions do not list shown as current-not-listed and not selectable again); effortOptions(tier) = '' plus the selected model's efforts; current tier = what the daemon resolves (tierSetting, src/config/analyze.ts:216, with parseTiering's leaf rules, src/config/analyze.ts:395-407): a configured effort leaf ('' included) always wins; a tier with a configured runner AND a non-empty model is that runner/model with the configured effort or none ('' = CLI default) — never the default's effort; any other tier (unset, model '' or a runner or model alone, which the daemon ignores) is the DEFAULT family's tier default with the configured effort, else the default's effort — a lone runner leaf is shown as ignored, and the tier stays clean until edited; selectRunner takes the new family's default for the tier, from sc3 fields only: tierDefaults[tier] with its effort when the model accepts it (CLI families); else toolLoopModel with no effort (the local family, which has no tierDefaults); else the family's first model with no effort; a family with no models cannot be selected; selectModel keeps the effort only if the new model accepts it, else clears it; collectWrites() = one whole-tier write {runner, model, effort} at ['models','tiers',tier] per dirty tier

Parity cases mirror the daemon's resolution: unset tier; runner+model with no effort (no effort); runner+model+effort; effort '' explicit; effort leaf alone on an unset tier; runner alone (ignored); model '' (unset); an alias model shown as its canonical id

Apply guard: collectWrites() refuses (Apply reports it and keeps the pending edit) any dirty tier whose model is not served by the loaded definitions — including an effort-only edit of a tier whose configured model is no longer listed; the user must pick a listed model first. So no unlisted model is ever written, approved or not
Regression fixture: a local family with toolLoopModel and no tierDefaults; switching a tier to it takes toolLoopModel with effort ''

Accepted-effort filtering at initialization too, as the registry does after tierSetting (src/daemon/model-registry.ts resolveTier → droppedEffort): a stored effort the resolved model does not accept is shown as '' (CLI default) with a note "stored effort '<e>' is not accepted by <model> — the daemon drops it"; the tier is NOT dirty for that, and the stored leaf is rewritten only when the user edits the tier (the whole-tier write then carries the shown effort)

api.name: ModelTiersSection check flow
api.signature: Check model… button → ModelCheckDialog(family, modelId) → Approve/Reject → restart offer

returns.meaning: Asks for a CLI family (from the definitions; Ollama is not offered) and a model id, runs checkModel off the EDT under a progress indicator, shows runs / input limit / per-effort verdict and evidence; Approve (with the non-rejected efforts the user ticks) or Reject records the decision; after an approval it offers 'Restart daemon': on a restart whose status read comes back running, the definitions are re-read, the section refreshes and the model is offered in that family; the tier is saved only by the normal Apply

errors.condition: the daemon's reason and detail, or the classified failure, shown in the dialog

postconditions: An unlisted model is never written to a tier (ac2)

api.name: restartRequired offer
api.signature: SettingsSection.takeRestartRequired(): Boolean = false; InsrcSettingsConfigurable.apply() offers one 'Restart daemon' prompt

returns.meaning: Each section that writes (ModelTiersSection, PerRoleSection, PerRepoSection) sets a flag when any of its writes returns Saved(restartRequired = true); takeRestartRequired() returns and clears it. InsrcSettingsConfigurable.apply() collects the generic table's Saved(restartRequired) results and every section's flag inside its background save loop, and AFTER the loop, on the EDT, offers ONE prompt when any successful write needed a restart — also when other writes failed (the prompt comes first, then the ConfigurationException listing the failures). Yes restarts through DaemonLifecycleCommandRunner.run(RESTART) under a progress indicator and confirms with daemonStatus(); the result is reported.

preconditions: Prompting and the restart run outside the background save loop
postconditions: One offer per Apply, not per tier

dataModelChanges.details: Kotlin mirror of the sc3 answer, parsed structurally in daemon/DaemonGateway.kt; no family, model or effort literal in the plugin.

NotRunning | OlderDaemon(text) | Other(text). The JetBrains transport (UnixSocketDaemonRpc.call) wraps every socket IOException — connect, write or read — as DaemonUnavailableException, so a broken connection is NotRunning, worded 'the daemon is not running or the connection was lost'; an empty or malformed reply is Other. The transport is reused unchanged.
Kotlin mirrors of sc4's ModelCheckResult and DecisionResult.
Saved gains restartRequired; Rejected gains detail. configWrite reads data.reason, data.detail and data.restartRequired.
Takes definitions instead of listsByProvider; PROVIDERS and leaf writes removed.

Per-tier runner/model state and writes removed. takeRestartRequired(): Boolean with a false default; implemented by the three writing sections and read by InsrcSettingsConfigurable.apply().
A default call(method, params, resultErrorIsFailure) overload; UnixSocketDaemonRpc.parse takes the flag.

Existing per-repo tier entries were already removed by the daemon's reconcile (s3); leaf-written global tiers read the same as whole-tier ones.

alternativesConsidered.name: Definitions-driven ModelTiersModel, whole-tier writes, check flow in the section
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep ModelTiersModel/ModelTiersSection as the JetBrains tier editor; feed them models.definitions; write each changed tier whole; unknown models go through models.check → approve/reject; per-repo tiers dropped.
alternativesConsidered.approach: DaemonGateway gains modelDefinitions(), modelsCheck(family, model), modelsApprove(checkId), modelsReject(checkId) over DaemonRpc, and its config.write result carries the daemon's reason, detail and restartRequired (SaveResult.Saved(restartRequired) / Rejected(reason, detail)). ModelTiersModel is built from a ModelDefinitions DTO instead of PROVIDERS + catalog enums + listModels: runner choices = families, model choices = that family's models (aliases shown, Ollama installed state), effort choices = the chosen model's efforts; the current tier = config overlaid on the family's tier default (same precedence as the daemon); a runner switch takes the family default; collectWrites emits one whole-tier write {runner, model, effort} at ['models','tiers',tier]. ModelTiersSection adds a 'Check model…' entry: models.check, a dialog with the per-effort verdicts and evidence, Approve (then save) / Reject; restartRequired offers a restart via DaemonLifecycleCommandRunner.run(RESTART). PerRepoOverridesModel/PerRepoSection keep only coreFloor and role tiers. Failures are classified (not running / disconnected / older daemon / other).
pros: Smallest shape that meets ac1-ac3: reuses the existing model/section split and the headless tests
Mirrors the s6 VS Code behaviour (same rules, same failure classes) so the two plugins agree
No new settings pages; native tier editing kept as decided
cons: ModelTiersModel's constructor and tests change substantially
The check dialog is Swing code that only a source scan / smoke test can cover headlessly

alternativesConsidered.name: Leaf writes kept, definitions only for choices
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Swap the option sources to models.definitions but keep field-by-field runner/model/effort writes.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Same gateway reads and check flow as a1, but collectWrites keeps writing ['models','tiers',tier,field] leaves; the daemon validates each leaf separately.
pros: Fewer changes to the write path and its tests
cons: A runner switch written as leaves passes through an invalid intermediate tier (new runner, old model) that the daemon may reject or briefly serve
Diverges from the CLI and VS Code whole-tier writes
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Leaf writes can pass through an invalid intermediate tier and diverge from the other clients.

alternativesConsidered.name: Shared definitions service with cache and a separate check dialog class
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: a1 plus an application-level ModelDefinitionsService caching the answer and a standalone ModelCheckDialog reused by other pages.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Introduce a project-independent service holding the last definitions answer, refreshed on demand, and a DialogWrapper subclass for check/approve; the settings section and any future surface consume both.
pros: Reusable if more JetBrains surfaces pick models later
cons: Adds a cache and service nobody asked for; a stale cache could offer a model the daemon no longer serves
More code and lifecycle than the Story needs
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Meets the criteria but adds a cache and service nobody asked for, with a stale-answer risk.
